blinding_guess.why: driver.py itself is self-consistent: constants 1-14 match the URScript prog in the same snapshot, and SERVOJ (9 ints), SET_PAYLOAD (2), STOPJ (1), JOINT_STATES (1+18), OUT and WAYPOINT_FINISHED framings agree with prog. But for SET_DIGITAL_OUT, SET_FLAG, SET_ANALOG_OUT and SET_TOOL_VOLTAGE driver.py sends the type code plus 2 ints while prog reads socket_read_binary_integer(1+6+1) (8 ints) after the type code, so the link is mis-framed; prog's count looks copied from the servoj branch, so the fault may lie on the other side rather than in this unit.

notes: The packet elements are integer message-type codes of the private TCP protocol between driver.py (TCP server on reverse_port) and the URScript program 'prog' that driver.py uploads to the robot on port 30002 (:923-927, :954). No .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition of these elements exists in the snapshot and they are not ROS interfaces, so definition_id is null for every port and the 'msg <pkg/Type>: <hash>' declares template cannot be filled; the 'api <symbol>: <declaration line>' template with the verbatim constant assignment was used for each provided element. msg_type repeats the packet's element type name (ur_driver/<CONSTANT>) because the code has no other type identifier for these messages. Wire layouts written/read by driver.py (all network-order int32 via struct '!i'): SERVOJ = [7, waypoint_id (always 999 at :772/:795), 6 x q*10000.0 (after subtracting URDF calibration joint_offsets, :446-448), t*1000000.0] = 9 ints; SET_PAYLOAD = [8, payload*1000.0] = 2 ints; SET_DIGITAL_OUT = [10, pin, value] = 3 ints; SET_ANALOG_OUT = [14, pin, value*1000000.0] = 3 ints; SET_FLAG = [12, pin, val] = 3 ints; SET_TOOL_VOLTAGE = [13, value, 0] = 3 ints where value is SetIO req.pin (:861); STOPJ = [6] = 1 int, and send_stopj is defined but never called in driver.py; incoming JOINT_STATES = code + 18 ints / 10000.0; OUT = code + string terminated by '~'; WAYPOINT_FINISHED = code + 1 int, read and discarded ('not handled'; set_waypoint_finished_cb stores a callback that is never invoked). Float values (servoj, payload, analog) are packed with 'i' and rely on Python 2 implicit float-to-int conversion. set_digital_out/set_analog_out/set_flag sleep IO_SLEEP_TIME = 0.05 s after sending, set_tool_voltage sleeps 0.55 s. QoS is null throughout: ROS 1, and these are raw TCP messages, not ROS topics. rate_hz 50.0 for SERVOJ comes from the 0.02 s timer and applies only while a trajectory is being sampled or its last point has not yet been sent. min_rate_hz 1.0 for JOINT_STATES is derived from the 1.0 s staleness check, which runs only when no socket data arrives within the 0.2 s select timeout. units for SET_TOOL_VOLTAGE are null: driver.py states none (io_interface.py, outside this unit, names the argument 'volts'); units entries for the other ports record the fixed-point scale factors the code applies, not physical units, which driver.py does not state. exclusive records the listening socket bound at :918 (allow_reuse_address = True at :517). references is limited to packet elements; driver.py also uses ROS interfaces outside the packet (topics joint_states, wrench, io_states; services ur_driver/setPayload and set_io; action follow_joint_trajectory). The URScript file prog was read only to understand the counterpart of this protocol; the IO read-count mismatch noted in blinding_guess is an observation about prog, not part of this unit's declaration. No dependency definition files were fetched.
